policies.description: Contact 14 days, mapping 30 days and individually identifiable raw notes 30 days; no 30–90 day unmatched-note interval
benefits: No identifiable notes after lookup expires
costs: 30 days may be too short for editorial consolidation
Human review and actual backup deletion still required
preconditions: Safe verified withdrawal method until lookup expiry
Aggregate only after documented deidentification review

policies.description: Contact 14 days, mapping 90 days, notes 90 days; preserves per-person lookup throughout proposed retention
benefits: No unmatched 30–90 day raw note interval by design
costs: Pseudonym linkage and potentially identifiable notes held 90 days
Strong token custody and deletion verification required
preconditions: Safe verified withdrawal method through end of note retention
Human review of storage, backup and legal requirements

policies.description: Do not retain individually identifiable raw notes or contact-mapping; a live non-recorded discussion or independently reviewed non-identifying aggregate only
costs: Weak per-question audit and variant attribution
If any genuinely nonidentifying aggregate is produced it may no longer be individually withdrawable
Aggregate eligibility and consent still require explicit review
preconditions: Specify what 'non-identifying' means and small-cell thresholds
No actual response storage until G1 approval
Participant communication about aggregate withdrawal limits

tokenProtocolProposal.scope: Participants would need a separate verifiable way to submit per-record withdrawal requests if notes are ever collected
guidance: Use fresh high-entropy single-purpose random token from a vetted cryptographic RNG, never derive it from name, birthday, email, session number or sequential ID
Store only securely derived verifier under separate restricted permissions and protect token distribution; never record raw tokens in logs, PR, analytics or GitHub
Avoid making mere possession a claim of real-world identity: implement clear bearer-token caveat, loss, theft, replay and incorrect-request handling
Provide expiry matching individual identifiable note retention, not only contact retention
Make verified requests an approval-controlled queue, never silent automated deletion or claim of success before storage and backup confirmation
Test constant-time comparison, rate limiting and secure redaction in any later actual implementation; these are requirements, not implemented features

changeHistory.before: D39: 14/30/90 with 30–90 day unmatched-note interval; D40: conceptual match assumed
changeHistory.after: Three alternative retention/withdrawal contracts; match/no-match model is synthetic, with explicit inability to issue identity proof or real deletion
changeHistory.reason: Eliminate contradictory proposal through human choice rather than claiming an automated fix
